> November 10: your generative strategy and your brand are approved in class. December 11: final review of the booklet, the revised GSM and the three Project 4 sheets.

**ARC 3133 · Architectural Visualization Methods 1** · Florida Atlantic University — School of Architecture  
Fall 2026 — Full Term · Tuesday, 5:00 PM–7:50 PM · Luis Pacheco Alcala and Christine Khouri Sader

*Build geometry with rules, vary it with data and communicate it through drawings, models and physical parts.*

## Welcome

Welcome to ARC 3133. This course is about describing architecture as a set of rules — operations, points and faces, arrays and fields — and turning that description into clear drawings, renders and physical objects: a CSG print, an attractor-driven façade and a store designed by a generative system.

We work mainly in Blender Geometry Nodes, and the video tutorials also cover Rhino + Grasshopper. No programming experience is needed: you build with nodes, and each lesson shows the same steps written as short pseudocode so you learn to read it.

## The semester

Arrays are taught in Weeks 6–7 with supported practice in Week 8, attractors in Week 9, fields in Week 10 and generative design in Week 11. Strategies and brands are approved in Week 12; Weeks 13 to 15 are working sessions on the three Project 4 sheets and the booklet, presented at the final review. Everything through Arrays was due by Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time, the mid-semester deadline.

## Four projects

| Project | What you do | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [P1 — GSM]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p1-gsm/) | Build a standardized graphic system through color theory, typography, composition and your own reusable template | 5% |
| [P2 — CSG]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p2-csg/) | Interpret real architecture through transformations and Boolean operations, explain it as instructions, then learn slicing and 3D printing | 15% |
| [P3 — Paneling]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p3-paneling/) | Build a reusable module from a documented panel system. Use lists, repetition, conditions and attractors to develop architectural studies | 30% |
| [P4 — Generative Store]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p4-generative-store/) | Design a system, not an output. Pick a generative strategy and a brand, build a system that produces stores of 40 to 64 m2, map its design space, select one result and present it as a competition-style sheet | 30% |

The midterm grade accumulates the Graphic Standards Manual, CSG sheet and print, module (3.1) and arrays (3.2). These assignments account for 40% of the final course grade. Report the accumulated result as a percentage of those 40 possible course points. The midterm adds no separate assessment weight. [Midterm grade calculation]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/overview/#midterm-grade)

## How we work

Each class is a short demonstration, then guided practice and critique. Bring your editable file every week: you should be able to change an input, predict what happens and explain why. Your Graphic Standards Manual sets the look of every sheet you present.

Project 2 ends in a 3D print; Project 4 ends in a competition-style sheet of a store your generative system produced. Complete the FabLab Safety Orientation before using any machine.
